<!-- thmbox-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:informal}
                                                   
Schedule-free SGD \eqref{schefree}, with an appropriate choice of parameters $\gamma, c_t, \kappa_t$, achieves optimal rates for nonsmooth and nonconvex $F$.
<!-- end thmbox-1 -->
<!-- assumption-1: body_md -->
\label{assump}
Let $F:\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function with the following properties:
\begin{itemize}

\item Let $\Delta_F \coloneqq F({\mathbf x}_0) -\inf_{{\mathbf x}} F({\mathbf x})$.

\item For any two points ${\mathbf x}$ and ${\mathbf w}$, $F({\mathbf x})-F({\mathbf w}) = \int_0^1 \left\langle \nabla F({\mathbf w}+t({\mathbf x}-{\mathbf w})),{\mathbf x}-{\mathbf w} \right\rangle\mathrm{d} t$. 

\item  $F$ is $G$-Lipshitz, \emph{i.e.}, for any point ${\mathbf x}$, $\left\|\nabla F({\mathbf x})\right\|\leq G$.
 
\end{itemize}
<!-- end assumption-1 -->
<!-- assumption-2: body_md -->
We assume access to a stochastic gradient oracle at any point ${\mathbf x}$. More formally, for any given point ${\mathbf x}$, each call to the oracle independently returns a stochastic gradient $\mathbf{g}$ that satisfies the following properties:
\[
\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{g}] = \nabla F({\mathbf x}), \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbb{E}\left[\left\|\mathbf{g} - \nabla F({\mathbf x})\right\|^2\right] \leq \sigma^2.
\]
We denote the stochastic gradient oracle as $\textsc{StoGrad}$. When the oracle returns the stochastic gradient $\mathbf{g}$ at point ${\mathbf x}$, we write this as $\mathbf{g} \gets \textsc{StoGrad}({\mathbf x})$.
<!-- end assumption-2 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:reg_station}
Suppose $F:\mathbb{R}^d\to \mathbb{R}$ is differentiable.
We say ${\mathbf x}$ is a $(\lambda,\varepsilon)$-stationary point of $F$ if $\left\| \nabla F({\mathbf x})\right\|^{[\lambda]}  \leq \varepsilon$, where 
\begin{align}
\left\| \nabla F({\mathbf x})\right\|^{[\lambda]} \coloneqq \inf_{\substack{p \in \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d),\\\mathbb{E}_{{\mathbf w}\sim p}[{\mathbf w}] ={\mathbf x}} } \left\{\left\|\mathbb{E}[\nabla F({\mathbf w})]\right\| + \lambda \cdot \mathbb{E}\left\|{\mathbf w}-{\mathbf x}\right\|^2 \right\}\,.
\end{align}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:convert}
If $F$ is $L$-smooth, then an $(L^2 \varepsilon^{-1},\varepsilon)$-stationary point ${\mathbf x}$ of $F$ satisfies $\left\|\nabla F({\mathbf x})\right\|\leq 2\varepsilon$. Moreover, if $F$ is $H$-second-order-smooth, then an $(H/2,\varepsilon)$-stationary point ${\mathbf x}$ of $F$ satisfies $\left\|\nabla F({\mathbf x})\right\|\leq 2\varepsilon$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
Consider the loss sequence $\ell_{1:T}$.
For any $T\geq 1$, we define the discounted regret of an online learner with respect to a comparator $\mathbf{u}$ as:
\begin{align}
{\sf Regret}^{[\beta
]}_T(\mathbf{u}) \coloneqq  \sum_{t=1}^T \beta^{T-t}\left( \ell_t({\boldsymbol \delta}_t)- \ell_t(\mathbf{u}) \right).
\end{align}
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{def:ema}
Given a discount factor $\beta \in (0,1)$ and a sequence of iterates $\{\mathbf{y}_s\}_{s=1}^t$, the $\beta$-EMA of the sequence up to time $t$, denoted as $\overline{\mathbf{y}}_t$, is defined as
\begin{align}
\overline{\mathbf{y}}_t = \frac{1-\beta}{1-\beta^t} \sum_{s=1}^t \beta^{t-s} \mathbf{y}_s.
\end{align}
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:random}
Let $\tau$ be a random index distributed over $\{1, 2, \dots, T\}$ with the following distribution:
\begin{align}
\Pr(\tau = t) = \begin{cases}
\frac{1 - \beta^t}{T}, & \text{for}~~ t = 1, \dots, T-1, \\
\frac{1}{1-\beta} \cdot \frac{1 - \beta^T}{T}, & \text{for}~~ t = T.
\end{cases}
\end{align}
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{def:stability}
Consider the iterates generated by \autoref{alg:general}.  The {iterate stability factor}, denoted by $C_{{\mathbf x}} \geq 0$, is the smallest nonnegative constant such that:
\begin{align*} 
\mathbb{E} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \|\mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{x}_{t-1}\|^2 \leq C_{{\mathbf x}} \cdot \mathbb{E} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \|{\boldsymbol \delta}_t\|^2.
\end{align*}
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:master}
Consider the iterates generated according to \autoref{alg:general}.
For $\beta \in (0, 1)$ and $D > 0$, define  the comparators for online learner as follows:
\begin{align}
\forall t \in[T], \quad \mathbf{u}_t \coloneqq -D \frac{\sum_{s=1}^{t} \beta^{t - s} \nabla F(\mathbf{y}_s)}{\left\|\sum_{s=1}^{t} \beta^{t - s} \nabla F(\mathbf{y}_s)\right\|}  .
\end{align}
Then, as long as the regularization strength satisfies $\mu \geq 8\lambda D \left(1 + { C_{{\mathbf x}}}{(1-\beta)^{-2}} \right)$, the following holds:
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}_{\tau }  \left\| \nabla F(\overline{\mathbf{y}}_{\tau})\right\|^{[\lambda]}  &\leq  \frac{ 1}{DT}\left(\beta \mathbb{E}\left[{\sf Regret}^{[\beta
]}_T(\mathbf{u}_T) \right] +  (1-\beta)\sum_{t=1}^{T}     \mathbb{E}\left[{\sf Regret}^{[\beta
]}_t(\mathbf{u}_t)\right]\right)    \\
&\quad + \frac{1}{DT} \mathbb{E} \sum_{t=1}^{T} (F({\mathbf x}_{t}) - F({\mathbf w}_{t}))    +  \frac{\mu D}{2}    + \frac{\sigma }{T\sqrt{1-\beta}}  + \sigma \sqrt{1-\beta}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
See \autoref{pf:lem:master}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:omd-regret}
Let $\beta \in (0,1)$, $\mu \geq 0$, $\eta > 0$, and a sequence of vectors $\{\mathbf{g}_t\}_{t=1}^T$. 
Suppose that $\mathbb{E}\left\|\mathbf{g}_t\right\|^2 \leq G^2 + \sigma^2$ for all $t\in[T]$. 
Consider an online learner initialized with ${\boldsymbol \delta}_1 = \bm{0}$ and updated as follows:
\begin{align} \tag{$\beta$-\textsf{OMD}}\label{exp:domd-og}
 {\boldsymbol \delta}_{t+1} = \frac{\beta}{1 + \eta \mu} \left( {\boldsymbol \delta}_{t} - \eta \mathbf{g}_t \right). 
\end{align}
Then, this online learner with  $\eta = \frac{2}{G + \sigma} \left\|\mathbf{u}\right\| \sqrt{1-\beta}$ achieves the following discounted regret bound:
\begin{align} \label{exp:discounted_regret}
 \mathbb{E}\left[{\sf Regret}^{[\beta
]}_T(\mathbf{u})\right] \leq \frac{2\left\|\mathbf{u}\right\|(G + \sigma)}{\beta\sqrt{1-\beta}} + \frac{\mu}{2}\left\|\mathbf{u}\right\|^2.
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
See \autoref{pf:lem:omd-regret}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- thmbox-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:opt}
Consider the iterates generated according to \autoref{alg:general}, where the online learner $\mathcal{A}$ achieves the discounted regret given by \eqref{exp:discounted_regret}. Let $\varepsilon > 0$ be such that $\varepsilon \leq \frac{7}{2}(G + \sigma)$ and let $T \geq 49 (G + \sigma)^2 \varepsilon^{-2}$. 
Then, there exists a choice of parameters $\beta=\beta_\star, D=D_\star, \mu=\mu_\star$  such that with $\overline{\mathbf{y}}_t$ and $\tau$ as specified by \autoref{def:ema} and \autoref{def:random}, the following holds:
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}_{\tau }  \left\| \nabla F(\overline{\mathbf{y}}_{\tau})\right\|^{[\lambda]} &\leq  3\varepsilon + \frac{ 1}{D_\star T}  \cdot \mathbb{E} \sum_{t=1}^{T} (F({\mathbf x}_{t}) - F({\mathbf w}_{t})) ,
                                                                                                                                                                         
\end{align*}
 The choice of parameters is summarized as follows:
\begin{itemize}[nosep]
\item The discounting factor is $\beta_\star = 1 - (\frac{\varepsilon}{7(G + \sigma)})^2$.
\item The comparator norm is $D_\star =    \frac{1}{4} \lambda^{-1/2} \varepsilon^{1/2} \left(1+\frac{49(G + \sigma)^2 }{\varepsilon^2} \sqrt{C_{{\mathbf x}}} \right)^{-1}   $.
\item The regularization strength is $\mu_\star = 2 \lambda^{1/2}\varepsilon^{1/2}  \left(1 + \frac{49(G + \sigma)^2 }{\varepsilon^2}\sqrt{C_{{\mathbf x}}}  \right)$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end thmbox-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
See \autoref{pf:thm:opt}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:momentum}
Consider the iterates of \autoref{alg:momentum}.
Under the setting of \autoref{thm:opt}, it holds that $\mathbb{E}_{\tau} \left\| \nabla F(\overline{\mathbf{y}}_{\tau})\right\|^{[\lambda]} \leq 4\varepsilon$,
provided that 
\begin{align} \label{rate:optimal}
T \geq \max \left\{ 392(G+\sigma)^2 \Delta_F\lambda^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-7/2} , ~~49 (G + \sigma)^2 \varepsilon^{-2} \right\}.
\end{align}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
With \autoref{alg:momentum}, the above inequalities, \eqref{ineq:sumF} and \eqref{ineq:cx}, show that $\sum_{t=1}^{T} \left(F({\mathbf x}_t) - F({\mathbf w}_t)\right) \leq \Delta_F$ and $C_{{\mathbf x}} \leq 1$. 
   Therefore, by applying \autoref{thm:opt}, we have 
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}_{\tau} \left[\left\| \nabla F(\overline{\mathbf{y}}_{\tau})\right\|^{[\lambda]}\right] &= 3\varepsilon +  \frac{4 \lambda^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-1/2}\left(1+\frac{49(G + \sigma)^2 }{\varepsilon^2}   \right)}{T} \leq 3\varepsilon +  \frac{4 \lambda^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-1/2}\left( 2\cdot\frac{ 49(G + \sigma)^2 }{\varepsilon^2}   \right)}{T} ,
\end{align*}
provided that $T \geq 49 (G + \sigma)^2 \varepsilon^{-2}$. From this, the iteration complexity bound \eqref{rate:optimal} follows.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:anchor}
Consider the iterates of \autoref{alg:anchor}.
Under the setting of \autoref{thm:opt}, the following holds:
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}_{\tau }  \left\| \nabla F(\overline{\mathbf{y}}_{\tau})\right\|^{[\lambda]}  \leq 3\varepsilon +  \frac{4\lambda^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-1/2}}{T}  \mathbb{E} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \left( F({\mathbf x}_0) - F({\mathbf w}_t) \right)   ,   
\end{align*}
provided that $T \geq 49 (G + \sigma)^2 \varepsilon^{-2}$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:anchor_complete}
Consider the iterates of \autoref{alg:anchor_complete}.
Under the setting of \autoref{thm:opt}, it holds that 
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}_{n \sim \mathrm{Unif}([N])}\mathbb{E}_{\tau} \left\| \nabla F(\overline{\mathbf{y}}^{(n)}_{\tau})\right\|^{[\lambda]} \leq 4\varepsilon,
\end{align}
provided that $N \geq 4\Delta_F \lambda^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-3/2}$ and $T \geq 49 (G + \sigma)^2 \varepsilon^{-2}$.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Applying \autoref{cor:anchor_complete} to each epoch $n$, we obtain:
\begin{align}
    \mathbb{E}_{\tau }  \left\| \nabla F(\overline{\mathbf{y}}_{\tau}^{(n)})\right\|^{[\lambda]}  
    &\leq 3\varepsilon +  \frac{4\lambda^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-1/2}}{T}  \mathbb{E} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \left( F(\mathbf{a}_n) - F({\mathbf w}^{(n)}_t) \right) \\
    &  =  3\varepsilon +   4\lambda^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-1/2}   \mathbb{E}   \left( F(\mathbf{a}_n) - F(\mathbf{a}_{n+1})  \right),
\end{align}
where the last equality follows because $\mathbf{a}_{n+1}$ is chosen uniformly at random from $\{{\mathbf w}^{(n)}_t\}_{t=1}^T$.

Summing over all epochs, since $\sum_{n=1}^N ( F(\mathbf{a}_n) - F(\mathbf{a}_{n+1})) =  F(\mathbf{a}_1) - F(\mathbf{a}_{N+1})$, we have:
\begin{align}
   \mathbb{E}_{n \sim \mathrm{Unif}([N])}\mathbb{E}_{\tau} \left\| \nabla F(\overline{\mathbf{y}}^{(n)}_{\tau})\right\|^{[\lambda]}   
   &\leq   3\varepsilon +   \frac{4\lambda^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-1/2}}{N}  \mathbb{E}   \left( F(\mathbf{a}_1) - F(\mathbf{a}_{N+1})  \right) \\
   &\leq 3\varepsilon +   \frac{4\lambda^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-1/2}\Delta_F}{N}.
\end{align}
Thus, setting $N \geq 4\Delta_F \lambda^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-3/2}$ ensures that the right-hand side is at most $4\varepsilon$.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:SF}
Consider the iterates of \autoref{alg:SF} with the parameter choices as in \autoref{thm:opt}, \emph{i.e.}, $\beta = \beta_\star$, $D = D_\star$, $\mu = \mu_\star$, and the parameters of \ref{exp:domd} chosen as:
\begin{align}
\eta = \eta_\star \coloneqq  \frac{2}{G + \sigma} D_\star \sqrt{1 - \beta_\star}\quad \text{and} \quad    \zeta= \zeta_\star \coloneqq \frac{\beta_\star}{1 + \eta_\star \mu_\star}.
\end{align} 
Then, it holds that $\mathbb{E}_{\tau} \left\| \nabla F(\overline{\mathbf{y}}_{\tau})\right\|^{[\lambda]} \leq 5\varepsilon$,
provided that 
\begin{align}  
T \geq \max \left\{ 980(G+\sigma)^2 \Delta_F\lambda^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-7/2} , ~~49 (G + \sigma)^2 \varepsilon^{-2} \right\}.
\end{align}
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
It is clear by definition that $C_{{\mathbf x}} = \frac{1}{\zeta_\star}$. Thus, the crux of the proof lies in controlling the sum of loss decrements by leveraging \eqref{exp:diff_SF} in  order to apply \autoref{thm:opt}.
In particular, we decompose the sum using the $G$-Lipschitz continuity of $F$ as follows:
\begin{align}
    \sum_{t=1}^{T} \left(F({\mathbf x}_t) - F({\mathbf w}_t)\right) &= \sum_{t=1}^{T} \left(F({\mathbf x}_{t}) - F({\mathbf w}_{t-1}) + F({\mathbf w}_{t-1}) - F({\mathbf w}_t)\right) \\
    &\leq \sum_{t=1}^{T} G \|{\mathbf x}_t - {\mathbf w}_{t-1}\| + \sum_{t=1}^{T} \left(F({\mathbf w}_{t-1}) - F({\mathbf w}_t)\right).
\end{align}
Applying the closeness property \eqref{exp:diff_SF} between ${\mathbf x}_t$ and ${\mathbf w}_{t-1}$, we can show that the first term in the upper bound is at most $\mathcal{O}\left(D_\star T \varepsilon\right)$, making it a lower-order term. 
For a complete proof, see \autoref{pf:cor:SF}.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:extrapolate}
Under \autoref{alg:SF} and using the extrapolated iterates defined in \eqref{def:zt}, the following holds:
\begin{align*}
{\mathbf z}_{t+1} - {\mathbf z}_{t} = -\frac{\eta}{1-\zeta}  \mathbf{g}_{t}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:parameters}
    With the parameter choices given in \autoref{cor:SF}, we have $\zeta = \zeta_\star = 1 - \Theta \left(\frac{\varepsilon^2}{(G + \sigma)^2} \right)$. Specifically, the parameters in schedule-free SGD are set as follows:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $\kappa_t$ is chosen uniformly from $[\zeta_\star, 1]$, implying that $1 - \Theta \left(\frac{\varepsilon^2}{(G + \sigma)^2}\right) \leq \kappa_t \leq 1$ for all $t$. This selection ensures that $\kappa_t$ remains close to $1$.
        \item The step size for the base SGD (${\mathbf z}$-trajectory) is set to $\frac{\eta_\star}{1-\zeta_\star}$, making it $\Theta\left(\frac{(G + \sigma)^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right)$ times larger than the OMD step size, $\eta_\star$.
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:first_term}
For  $\beta\in(0,1)$, consider the iterates generated as per \autoref{alg:general}.
                                                             
                                  
                                                                          
             
Consider the following definitions:
\begin{itemize}
\item For each $t \in [T]$, let   $\mathbf{u}_t \coloneqq -D \frac{\sum_{s=1}^t\beta^{t-s}\nabla F(\mathbf{y}_s)}{\left\|\sum_{s=1}^t\beta^{t-s}\nabla F(\mathbf{y}_s)\right\|}$. 
\item For each $t \in [T]$, let $\mathbf{Y}_t$ be the random iterate distributed over $\{\mathbf{y}_s\}_{s=1}^t$ as:
\begin{align*}
\Pr(\mathbf{Y}_t= \mathbf{y}_s) = q_{t,s} \coloneqq \beta^{t-s} \cdot \frac{1-\beta}{1-\beta^t} \quad \text{for $s=1,2,\dots, t$.}
\end{align*} 
\end{itemize}Then, the following upper bound holds:
\begin{align*} 
\mathbb{E}_{\tau }   \left\|\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}_{\tau}}\nabla F(\mathbf{Y}_{\tau})\right\|  &\leq  \frac{\beta   \mathbb{E}\left[{\sf Regret}^{[\beta
]}_T(\mathbf{u}_T) \right] +  (1-\beta)\sum_{t=1}^{T}     \mathbb{E}\left[{\sf Regret}^{[\beta
]}_t(\mathbf{u}_t)\right]}{DN}  - \frac{\mu\mathbb{E} \sum_{t=1}^T   \left\|{\boldsymbol \delta}_t\right\|^2}{2DT}  \\
&\quad +\frac{\mathbb{E} \sum_{t=1}^{T} (F({\mathbf x}_{t}) - F({\mathbf w}_{t}))}{DT}     + \frac{\sigma \beta}{T\sqrt{1-\beta}}  + \sigma \sqrt{1-\beta}+     \frac{\mu D}{2}  .
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
See \autoref{pf:lem:first_term}.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:second_term}
For  $\beta\in(0,1)$, consider the iterates generated as per \autoref{alg:general}
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}_{\tau}  \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}_{\tau}} \left\|\mathbf{Y}_{\tau} - \overline{\mathbf{y}}_{\tau}\right\|^2  \leq   
\frac{2}{T} \mathbb{E}\sum_{t=1}^{T} \left\|{\boldsymbol \delta}_t\right\|^2 +  \frac{4\beta }{(1-\beta)^2T } \mathbb{E}\sum_{t=1}^T \left\|{\mathbf x}_t-{\mathbf x}_{t-1}\right\|^2.
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
See \autoref{pf:var_gen}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:backbone}
For  $\beta\in(0,1)$, consider the iterates generated as per \autoref{alg:general}.
                                                                                 
Consider the following definitions:
\begin{itemize}
\item For each $t \in [T]$, let   $\mathbf{u}_t \coloneqq -D \frac{\sum_{s=1}^t\beta^{t-s}\nabla F(\mathbf{y}_s)}{\left\|\sum_{s=1}^t\beta^{t-s}\nabla F(\mathbf{y}_s)\right\|}$. 
\item For each $t \in [T]$, let $\mathbf{Y}_t$ be the random iterate distributed over $\{\mathbf{y}_s\}_{s=1}^t$ as:
\begin{align*}
\Pr(\mathbf{Y}_t= \mathbf{y}_s) = q_{t,s} \coloneqq \beta^{t-s} \cdot \frac{1-\beta}{1-\beta^t} \quad \text{for $s=1,2,\dots, t$.}
\end{align*} 
\end{itemize}
Then, for any $n\in [T]$, we have 
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}\sum_{t=1}^{n} \beta^{n-t}(F({\mathbf w}_{t}) - F({\mathbf x}_{t})) &\leq    -D \frac{1-\beta^n}{1-\beta}  \mathbb{E} \left\|\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}_n}\nabla F(\mathbf{Y}_n)\right\| +\frac{\sigma D}{\sqrt{1-\beta}} \\
&\quad +\mathbb{E}
[{\sf Regret}^{[\beta
]}_n(\mathbf{u}_n)]   +\mathbb{E}   \sum_{t=1}^n   \beta^{n-t} ( - \frac{\mu}{2}\left\|{\boldsymbol \delta}_t\right\|^2 + \frac{\mu}{2}D^2).
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
See \autoref{pf:lem:backbone}.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:var_decomp}
For each $n \in [T]$ the following holds:
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}_{n}} \left\|\mathbf{Y}_{n} - \overline{\mathbf{y}}_{n}\right\|^2 \leq 2\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{X}_{n}} \left\|\mathbf{X}_{n} - \overline{\mathbf{x}}_{n}\right\|^2 +  2\sum_{s=1}^{n} q_{n,s} \left\|\mathbf{y}_s - {\mathbf x}_s\right\|^2.
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
See \autoref{pf:lem:var_decomp}.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:var1}
The following holds:
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}_{\tau}  \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{Y}_{\tau}} \left\|\mathbf{X}_{\tau} - \overline{\mathbf{x}}_{\tau}\right\|^2  \leq    \frac{2\beta }{(1-\beta)^2 T} \sum_{n=1}^T \left\|{\mathbf x}_n-{\mathbf x}_{n-1}\right\|^2.
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
See \autoref{pf:lem:var1}.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop1:var1}
For each $n \in [T]$, it holds that 
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{X}_n} \left\|\mathbf{X}_n - \overline{\mathbf{x}}_n\right\|^2 \leq 2\sum_{t=1}^n \lambda_{n,t} \left\|{\mathbf x}_{t}- {\mathbf x}_{t-1}\right\|^2, \quad \text{where}~\lambda_{n,t} \coloneqq\sum_{i=t}^n\sum_{j=1}^{t-1}  q_{n,i} q_{n,j}  (i-j) .
\end{align*}
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Let us fix $n \in [T]$. 
Let $\widehat{\mathbf{X}}_n$ be an independent copy of $\mathbf{X}_n$. Then, by Jensen's inequality, we get:
\begin{align}
\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{X}_n} \left\|\mathbf{X}_n - \overline{\mathbf{x}}_n\right\|^2  &= 
\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{X}_n} \left\|\mathbf{X}_n - \mathbb{E}_{\widehat{\mathbf{X}}_n}[\widehat{\mathbf{X}}_n]\right\|^2  \leq  
\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{X}_n, \widehat{\mathbf{X}}_n} \left\|\mathbf{X}_n - \widehat{\mathbf{X}}_n\right\|^2  \\
&= 2 \sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{j=1}^{i-1} q_{n,i} q_{n,j} \left\|{\mathbf x}_i- {\mathbf x}_{j}\right\|^2\,.  
\end{align}
Next, using Cauchy-Schwartz and triangle inequality, we get:
\begin{align*}
\left\|{\mathbf x}_i- {\mathbf x}_{j}\right\|^2 \leq \left(\sum_{t=j+1}^i \left\|{\mathbf x}_{t}-{\mathbf x}_{t-1}\right\|\right)^2 \leq (i-j) \sum_{t=j+1}^i \left\|{\mathbf x}_t-{\mathbf x}_{t-1}\right\|^2.
\end{align*}
Hence, it follows that
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{X}_n} \left\|\mathbf{X}_n - \overline{\mathbf{x}}_n\right\|^2 &\leq 2 \sum_{i=1}^n \sum_{j=1}^{i-1}  \sum_{t=j+1}^i q_{n,i} q_{n,j}  (i-j)  \left\|{\mathbf x}_t-{\mathbf x}_{t-1}\right\|^2 \\
&= 2 \sum_{t=1}^n \left(\sum_{i=t}^n\sum_{j=1}^{t-1}  q_{n,i} q_{n,j}  (i-j)  \right) \left\|{\mathbf x}_t-{\mathbf x}_{t-1}\right\|^2 
\end{align*}
This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop2:var1}  
For $1\leq t\leq n\leq T$, it holds that 
\begin{align*}
\lambda_{n,t} \leq  \frac{(n-t+1) \beta^{n-t+1}}{1-\beta^n}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
In order to prove the desired upper bound, let us first simplify the expression for $\lambda_{n,t}$ as follows:
\begin{align*}
\lambda_{n,t} &= \left(\frac{1-\beta}{1-\beta^n}\right)^2 \cdot \sum_{i=t}^n\sum_{j=1}^{t-1}  \beta^{n-i} \beta^{n-j} (i-j)\\
&= \left(\frac{1-\beta}{1-\beta^n}\right)^2 \cdot \sum_{i=t}^n\sum_{\delta=i-t+1}^{i-1}  \beta^{n-i} \beta^{n-i+\delta} \delta &&(\delta\coloneqq i-j)\\
&= \left(\frac{1-\beta}{1-\beta^n}\right)^2 \cdot \sum_{k=0}^{n-t}\sum_{\delta=n-k-t+1}^{n-k-1}  \beta^{k} \beta^{k+\delta} \delta &&(k\coloneqq n-i)\\
&= \left(\frac{1-\beta}{1-\beta^n}\right)^2 \cdot \sum_{k=0}^{n-t}\left[\beta^{2k}\sum_{\delta=n-k-t+1}^{n-k-1}   \delta\beta^{\delta}  \right].
\end{align*}
Next, let us compute the inner summation:
\begin{align*}
\sum_{\delta=n-k-t+1}^{n-k-1}   \delta\beta^{\delta} &=  \beta \cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\beta} \sum_{\delta=n-k-t+1}^{n-k-1}  \beta^{\delta} = \beta \cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}\beta} \left( \frac{\beta^{n-k-t+1} - \beta^{n-k}}{1-\beta}
\right) \\
&= \frac{\beta^{a-k+1} - \beta^{b-k+1}}{(1-\beta)^2} + \frac{(a-k) \beta^{a-k} -(b-k) \beta^{b-k}}{1-\beta}. &&(a \coloneqq n-t+1,~ b\coloneqq n)
\end{align*}
Substituting this back to the above expression for $\lambda_{n,t}$, we have
\begin{align*}
\lambda_{n,t}  &= \left(\frac{1-\beta}{1-\beta^n}\right)^2 \cdot \sum_{k=0}^{n-t} \beta^{2k} \left[ \frac{\beta^{a-k+1} - \beta^{b-k+1}}{(1-\beta)^2} + \frac{(a-k) \beta^{a-k} -(b-k) \beta^{b-k}}{1-\beta} \right]\\
&= \left(\frac{1-\beta}{1-\beta^n}\right)^2 \cdot \sum_{k=0}^{n-t}   \left[ \left(\frac{\beta^{a+1} -\beta^{b+1}}{(1-\beta)^2} + \frac{a\beta^a -b\beta^b}{1-\beta}\right) \beta^k   - \frac{\beta^a -\beta^b}{1-\beta}k\beta^k \right].
\end{align*}
Now one can compute the first and second terms above using the following identities:
\begin{itemize}
\item First term: note that $\sum_{k=0}^{n-t} \beta^k = \frac{1-\beta^{n-t+1}}{1-\beta} = \frac{1-\beta^a}{1-\beta}$.
\item Second term: note that $\sum_{k=0}^{n-t} k\beta^k = \beta \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} \beta} \left( \frac{1-\beta^a}{1-\beta}\right) =\frac{\beta -\beta^{a+1}}{(1-\beta)^2} - \frac{a\beta^a}{1-\beta}$.
\end{itemize}
Thus, it follows that
\begin{align*}
\lambda_{n,t}   
&= \left(\frac{1-\beta}{1-\beta^n}\right)^2 \cdot   \left[ \left(\frac{\beta^{a+1} -\beta^{b+1}}{(1-\beta)^2} + \frac{a\beta^a -b\beta^b}{1-\beta}\right)\cdot  \frac{1-\beta^a}{1-\beta}   - \frac{\beta^a -\beta^b}{1-\beta} \cdot \left( \frac{\beta -\beta^{a+1}}{(1-\beta)^2} - \frac{a\beta^a}{1-\beta}\right)  \right]\\
&= \frac{ (\beta^{a+1}-\beta^{b+1}) \frac{1-\beta^a}{1-\beta} + (a \beta^a -b\beta^b)(1-\beta^a) - (\beta^{a+1}-\beta^{b+1}) \frac{1-\beta^a}{1-\beta }  + (\beta^a-\beta^b) a\beta^a}{(1-\beta^n)^2}\\
&= \frac{   (a \beta^a -b\beta^b)(1-\beta^a)  + (\beta^a-\beta^b) a\beta^a}{(1-\beta^n)^2} =  \frac{  a\beta^a (1-\beta^b) -b\beta^b(1-\beta^a)}{(1-\beta^n)^2} \leq \frac{  a\beta^a (1-\beta^b)  }{(1-\beta^n)^2}.
\end{align*}
Upon plugging back the definition of $a$ and $b$, this completes the proof of \autoref{prop2:var1}.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
